items.title: Mozambique: Chapo reaffirms commitment to strengthening diplomatic ties with international partners
items.summary: The President was speaking on Thursday at a ceremony in which he received newly accredited diplomatic representatives, highlighting investment, business cooperation, technology transfer and skills development as priorities for promoting economic and social development According to Maria Lucas, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Chapo welcomed the accreditation of the new representatives and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to strengthening relations of friendship and cooperation with the countries and institutions they represent The diplomats are Martin Hackelberg from Germany, Brieu Pont from France, Lianne Houben from the Netherlands, Francisco Pardo from the European Union (EU), Ayça İnam from Türkiye, Dato Yusof from Malaysia, Roland Beridze from Georgia, Yury V. Nikalaichyk from Belarus, and Rod Rembendambya from Gabon During his meeting with the German representative, Chapo said Mozambique intended to sign a new technical cooperation framework agreement with Germany soon.

items.title: Academia urged to present solutions for development challenges
items.summary: Maputo, 23 Oct (AIM) – The Minister of Agriculture, Roberto Mito, has challenged Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM), Mozambique’s oldest higher education institution, to produce scientific guidance that will enable the construction of a resilient economy capable of bringing solutions to the country’s development challenges. Speaking on Thursday at the “First Symposium on Climate Adaptation and Resilience in Mozambique”, held in Maputo, the minister said that the challenge is for the entire Mozambican academic community and if “measures are implemented, they would help the nation reduce its reliance on external funding.” “Science should play a central role in identifying alternatives for national development, helping the country to leverage its existing resources and transform them into a means of financing its own priorities. Mozambique needs to rethink how it mobilizes resources for development and external funding should not come at the expense of the nation’s own capacity to find answers to its challenges.We must find local solutions to address local problems”, he said.

items.title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
items.summary: Medics at el-Fasher's Saudi Hospital performed a Caesarean by phone light on the day it was bombed A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings The health minister of the group's civilian-affiliated government dismissed the allegations as propaganda Dr Alaa Eldin Nugud said it was a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times Under international law it is illegal to attack…

items.title: Why a student protest movement is challenging 12 years of Vučić rule in Serbia
items.summary: Young Serbians have been the driving force behind the movement, but none of the candidates are students Final campaign rallies have taken place across Serbia, ahead of a snap election billed as a referendum on the country's future After two years of student protests, Serbians vote for a new parliament on Sunday in elections that threaten populist leader Aleksandar Vučić's 12 years in power The main threat to Vučić's dominance in Serbian politics comes from a two-year-old student movement, but there are concerns surrounding the fairness of the vote They have no obvious leaders and are not used to politics, but the "Student List-Students Win" movement has attracted anti-government voters across Serbia The Student List is fielding candidates from across Serbian society - and as he joined students marching towards Belgrade, lead candidate and cardiologist Ilija Srdanović said history was being rewritten: "The energy is unstoppable." items.title: South Korea proposes military talks with North again
items.summary: South Korea is attempting to mutually determine the land border with North Korea amid military incidents and escalating tensions South Korea's Defense Ministry on Friday proposed military talks with North Korea in an attempt to "mutually confirm the precise location" of their border and discuss restoring communication channels The ministry said it had proposed talks last November to resolve differences over the line, and reduce the risk of accidental deaths, but Pyongyang had not responded The latest proposal, announced by Deputy Minister for National Defense Policy Kim Hong-cheol, follows a landmine blast in the demiliterized zone (DMZ) in September that injured three South Korean soldiers North Korean troops have been building tactical roads, fences and been laying mines in the DMZ in the recent years. South Korea's Kim said the North's troops have repeatedly crossed the line in the process Seoul's military also concluded that North Korea had buried mines south of the Military Demarcation Line (MDL) which caused the recent blast.

items.title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
items.summary: Nearly 5,000 healthcare workers have been trained to deal with Ebola Kenya is grappling with its first ever outbreak of Ebola, a disease which neighbouring countries, such as Uganda and Democratic Republic of Congo, are used to dealing with Nine cases have now been confirmed including its first patient, who travelled from DR Congo and died two weeks ago Four relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner have now tested positive, meaning they are all linked to him But concerns are rising that the virus could start spreading further, even as the government has sought to assure citizens The US has warned it citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert Kenyans have been expressing their concerns that the disease could spread more widely More than 4,000 people have died since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according…
